name: yuna
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one standalone Kalistar illustration, never a card or contact sheet. Deliver a true 4:5 portrait, ideally 1024 x 1280, edge-to-edge painting. Image 1 Momo is the primary STYLE reference: visible rich brushwork, large painted color planes, narrative emotion, worn material, controlled edges. Image 2 Valazar is secondary STYLE reference for volumes and textured materials, NOT an instruction to make every scene gloomy. Image 3 is IDENTITY reference only: preserve recognizable FF10 face/hair/costume cues but DO NOT copy its portrait pose, smooth rendering, white background or anime stylization. Render the face with the SAME textured, mature painterly treatment as the Kalistar references, natural eye scale, no anime or photographic skin.
Composition: a 737 x 921 card-art window will contain this image. Keep face and main hands within central x20-78%; all essential equipment within x18-80%. Show full body or generous three-quarter figure with margin above head, enough breathing room below action and lateral margins. Character is large and legible, not tiny. Main contrast on face and story gesture. Restrained evocative background with broad values, no dense crowd. Coherent anatomy: one head, exactly two arms and two legs; coherent hands, contacts and continuous equipment.
No text, numbers, lettering, logos, watermark, card frame, barcode, interface, photo, polished 3D, manga, artificial glamor pose, extra limbs, uniform digital noise. This is an original scene interpretation, not a copied game screenshot.
Subject and scene: Yuna from the ORIGINAL FINAL FANTASY X, a dignified 17-year-old summoner, ordinarily fully clothed and nonsexual. The sending dance over the shallow water at Kilika after the disaster, at violet-peach dusk. Her short chestnut-brown bob and long beaded blue earring match the identity reference; her right eye green and left eye blue, discreet and natural. Canonical first-game outfit: white crossover kimono-style upper panels over a black halter underbodice, yellow patterned obi with blue rear bow, purple long floral skirt, detached long flowing white sleeves fading to pale pink. NO FFX-2 outfit. In a graceful quiet turning step, both hands hold the SAME continuous slim ceremonial staff; one hand at chest height and the other near waist, believable grip, shaft rising slightly diagonally within the safe zone. The complete iconic staff head, a gold circular openwork ring with purple-red inner detail, is clearly visible above her shoulder but below top margin; staff bottom also visible. Face turned three-quarter toward the last drifting soul-lights, melancholy compassion and courage, brows tender, lips gently parted, eyes readable. A handful of delicate pale pyreflies rise from the reflected water near her; these are subtle lights, not a heavy magical storm. Simplified damaged wooden pier and tropical shore far behind, no corpses or gore. Weightless sleeve motion, embroidered cloth and wet ripples painted with tangible brushstrokes. Warm twilight reflected on her face against cooler water. The illustration tells care and loss, not battle or fashion modeling.
